name: EPFL memory-controller, LUT-6 count
description: Optimise the EPFL combinational benchmark circuit memory-controller (a memory controller; 1204 inputs, 1231 outputs) with the logic-synthesis tool ABC and map it to lookup tables (LUTs) with at most 6 inputs, minimising the number of LUTs. The result must compute the same function as the original circuit.
contract: script() -> string of ABC commands separated by `;` or newlines. The evaluator runs `read <circuit>; <script>` in ABC and writes out the network the script leaves. That network must consist only of LUTs with at most 6 inputs (in ABC a LUT mapper such as `if -K 6` produces one; library gates or a wider node are invalid), and it must be equivalent to the original circuit, which a separate ABC process checks with `cec`. The script may not contain the characters ! / \ ~, may not use commands that read or write files, change the session or start other programs (read*, write*, load*, dump*, save* and their short forms, source, alias, set, unset, history, cd, ls, pwd, quit, exit), and may not ask for LUTs wider than 6 inputs (-K above 6). Time limits: 1200 s for the script, 900 s for the equivalence check. A script that is refused, fails, runs out of time or changes the function is invalid. Score: the number of LUTs with two or more inputs (buffers, inverters and constants are not counted), minimized.
notes: EPFL combinational benchmark 'Memory controller' (1204 inputs, 1231 outputs; Amaru, Gaillardon and De Micheli, IWLS 2015, tables I and II): the combinational part of a memory controller taken from OpenCores. The task maps it to 6-input LUTs and scores the LUT count.
Most records come from SAT-based exact synthesis of subcircuits, which an ABC script cannot express.
Requires the Berkeley ABC binary (set ARNEW_ABC).
LUTs and levels are counted from the written network by the convention of the EPFL table (single-input nodes are free), not from ABC's print_stats.

science_relevance.reason: The cited papers have LUT technology mapping and the minimisation of benchmark circuits as their main objective, and the evaluator scores exactly the LUT count or level count of an equivalence-checked 6-LUT network; the local candidate is an ABC script, which is narrower than the methods of the record holders.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Implement the EPFL benchmark circuit mem_ctrl as a network of lookup tables with at most six inputs, with an ABC command script, minimising the size (LUT count for size, LUT levels for depth).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Mapping logic to k-input lookup tables fixes the area and delay of an FPGA implementation, and the EPFL suite is the community reference for logic optimisation, with best LUT-6 counts and levels lowered by new synthesis methods every few years. A better result is a smaller or shallower implementation of a standard circuit; the best-known networks mostly come from SAT-based exact synthesis, which a script of ABC commands cannot express.
